scope: Six stranded members assessed independently; the three enclosing archive convictions are retained without re-judgment.
safety: All behavior conclusions derive from static source, call/control-flow review and native disassembly/decryption. No specimen, destructive command or recovered script was executed; no payload endpoint was contacted.

members.marker_note: Installer: credential theft and persistence; naming coverage added
evidence: The arm64 entry at 0x100000690 calls the command-producing helper, obtains its C string, and calls system at 0x1000006b8. This is executable code, not an unused string.

At 0x100000748 the helper copies 0x90dc bytes from __const. It passes the following 37077 encrypted bytes and seed 0x11667 to crypt. The crypt loop XORs each byte with the low state byte and updates state using ((state * 0x3785) & 0xffffffff) % 35999. The modulus is parsed from embedded 09:59:59. Reimplementation recovers an osascript -e command without executing the specimen.

The command joins quoted lines with AppleScript return, then runs the resulting script. Its final call invokes f7067467169335976972. Numeric handler renaming is an independent concealment technique, beyond the already detected XOR command hiding.

The main handler obtains USER, creates a random /tmp staging directory, queries system_profiler, reads a cached password, validates it with dscl . authonly, or repeatedly shows a masked Installation password dialog. It caches the password and adds it to the collection directory.

Copy helpers bind source and destination arguments, create destination directories, read the source, and run cat into the destination. Browser loops select Default/Profile directories and collect Cookies, Login Data, Web Data, Local Extension Settings and IndexedDB. Gecko routines copy cookies.sqlite, formhistory.sqlite, key4.db and logins.json and locate MetaMask IndexedDB using prefs.js.

It copies login.keychain-db and a UUID-named Keychains folder; desktop wallet directories; Notes SQLite files and attachments. Finder automation copies protected stores and Desktop/Documents files selected by extensions with a 10 MiB cumulative limit. Notes scripting is a fallback when the SQLite copy is empty.

The staged directory is packed with ditto into /tmp/out.zip; the upload helper sends that same ZIP with curl --data-binary to an HTTP host configured in the main handler. It then deletes the stage and ZIP. This links targeted acquisition, staging, transport and cleanup.

After theft it checks Ledger Live.app, downloads a replacement ZIP, terminates Ledger Live, removes the original with a sudo-fed password and extracts into /Applications. A later helper fetches a command, inserts it into a RunAtLoad/KeepAlive LaunchDaemon, uses sudo to install and bootstrap it, and falls back to nohup. The daemon UserName is the current user, so this does not prove the downloaded command runs as root.

The enclosing package postinstall disables Gatekeeper and removes quarantine before opening Installer and a bundled Archicad patch. These are deployment context from a separate script, not behaviors attributed to Installer bytes.
members.limits_and_judgment: No execution, user-consent history, AppleEvents grants, administrator authorization, successful upload or final downloaded stage was observed. The implemented credential theft, deceptive password handling and unwanted replacement/persistence establish the verdict independently.

members.marker_note: parser-session writer: exports environment and evaluates HTTP reply
evidence: getMacAddress enumerates os.networkInterfaces(), selects external IPv4 interface entries and returns their MAC addresses. Module initialization copies all process.env entries into data alongside platform, hostname, username and the MAC list.
g replaces each hex pair with String.fromCharCode(parseInt(pair,16)). The table decodes to require, axios, post, an HTTPS endpoint, headers, an X-header name/value and then.

The exported function resolves require(hl[1])[[hl[2]]] as axios.post, sends data as its second argument, supplies the concealed header object, follows the decoded then property and evaluates r.data. An empty catch discards failures. Neither full-environment export nor server-response evaluation serves the advertised HTTP middleware/logging purpose.

The archive entrypoint declares this package as CommonJS, and calls a writer at load time using a non-relative .pnpm/httpreslog path. The listed writer itself requires ../package.json, which resolves to a src/package.json absent from the archive. These resolution problems can prevent execution in a normal standalone install; they do not make the explicitly implemented theft and reply evaluator benign.
members.limits_and_judgment: No live endpoint, server response or resolving deployment environment was observed. Module-resolution defects limit reachability, not the malicious nature of its code.

members.marker_note: osinthell v.js: silently deletes Windows System32 DLLs
evidence: An exported zero-argument function invokes child_process.execSync with del /F /S /Q targeting C:\Windows\System32\*.dll, shell:true and stdio:ignore, then swallows errors.

This is a forced recursive system-DLL sweep, not deletion of the package own files or a named obsolete DLL. The package entrypoint calls v() from its sorgu operation alongside the other destructive modules.
members.limits_and_judgment: No caller invocation or Windows privilege level was observed; locked files and access controls may limit deletion. Its implemented system-wide target and concealed failure handling tip the verdict.

members.marker_note: osinthell f.js: zeroes the physical boot sector before MBR repair
evidence: The exported function opens \\.\PhysicalDrive0 with r+, allocates 512 zero bytes, writes that buffer to the same descriptor at absolute position zero and closes it. The data and handle are explicitly linked by variables.

After swallowing errors it separately invokes bootrec /fixmbr with ignored output. That repair command is dual-use and remains notable. It does not restore the partition table destroyed by zeroing the entire first sector. There is no backup or legitimate partitioning workflow in this module.
members.limits_and_judgment: No administrator rights, writable physical device or successful write was observed. The explicit sector-zeroing operation tips the verdict despite the later repair attempt.

members.marker_note: osinthell p.js: truncates regular files across Windows drive roots
evidence: The exported function iterates hardcoded C:, D:, E: and F: roots, reads each directory, joins each returned entry to its root, checks statSync(full).isFile(), then writes an empty string to that same full path.

writeFileSync has only two arguments, so its default write mode truncates an existing regular file. All failures are swallowed. The sweep covers regular files immediately at the roots; it does not recursively empty every directory.
members.limits_and_judgment: No mounted drive contents or permissions were observed. Unconditional empty overwrites of root-level user/system files across multiple drives tip the verdict.

members.marker_note: osinthell t.js: disables boot recovery and ignores boot failures
evidence: The exported function calls the imported execSync twice: bcdedit /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures, then bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No.

Both calls select a real shell, ignore child streams and discard caught failures. Together they inhibit automatic boot recovery without a repair or restoration workflow. They are called from the package sorgu entrypoint.
members.limits_and_judgment: No elevation or successful BCD modification was observed. Hardcoded recovery disablement inside the destructive utility tips the verdict.

rule_changes.admission: At least eight AppleScript handler declarations with a one-letter prefix and 16-20 decimal digits. A single numeric name, seven such handlers, normal names or calls without declarations do not qualify. Matches recovered native command text as well as scripts. Suspicious, not hostile.
rule_changes.preservation: All 15 relocated definitions were compared after applying the ID map: defaults, file types, platform gates, criticality, matchers, exception logic and consumers are preserved. No rule was weakened, deleted semantically or reduced in severity. Existing target configure leaf grows from 73 to 88 rules; no new taxonomy leaf or capacity exception is introduced.
rule_changes.consumer_audit: Inspected every exact reference and ancestor selector of the old and new launchd homes. No direct old plist/ or new configure/ directory selector exists; common os/service and os ancestors retain membership. Updated live fixture contracts; dated historical scan reports retain their old IDs. New function-name rule has macOS/source-type gates; JavaScript and PE consumers cannot gain same-file matches from it. Package-scope consumers still require their independent attack-admission legs.

checks.native_x86_control: The existing x64-helper-updated-state-byte-xor rule still matches the extracted x86-64 slice; the arm64 counterpart matches fresh standalone analysis.
checks.note: The oct24 check.py harness scans its own source/report and erroneously searches all rendered JSON for the phrase validation failed. Its 22 actual fixture files were therefore passed explicitly to the analyzer; all 43 case assertions pass.

classifier_disagreements: All four standalone osinthell modules remain ML BENIGN before and after, despite unchanged accurate hostile rules. Their containing archive remains HOSTILE. Features v18 are older than analyzer feature schema v21; no duplicate or inflated trait was added to manipulate those results.
material_detection_losses: None in paired fresh scans after normalizing the 15 relocated IDs. Initial cached universal-Mach-O scans differed in selected architecture and composite/low-tier findings; controlled original-versus-revised scans show zero losses for both standalone Installer and every enclosing-archive member.
